events.description: UN Monitoring Team releases 14th report under 1988 sanctions regime, first covering a full year of Taliban rule; Taliban issue blanket denial
Ayman al-Zawahiri killed in Kabul in a guesthouse associated with Sirajuddin Haqqani; Taliban never admitted he was there
Taliban takeover of Afghanistan; Haqqanis move on Kabul and seize interior ministry and intelligence; prisons broken open releasing ISKP members
Previous UN Monitoring Team Afghanistan report (13th) written, covering May 2021 - early 2022, Fitton-Brown's last
Mullah Abdul Qayyum Zakir released from Guantanamo; shortly after took over Taliban military in the south
Mullah Omar died; Taliban leadership issued statements in his name until exposed in 2015
After exposure of Omar's death, factions incl. Mullah Yaqoob briefly broke away; Sirajuddin and Jalaluddin Haqqani reunited the Taliban behind Hibatullah's predecessor/new leadership
US military issued a ~$75,000 reward for Sirajuddin Haqqani (first public mention)
Unconfirmed reports that ISKP leader Sanaullah Ghafari was killed, possibly in an engagement with the Taliban
Reports (dismissed by host) that Baradar and Siraj Haqqani came to blows, even that Baradar was killed
Turnover of Taliban prime minister; previous PM said to be sick
TTP insurgency killed ~100,000 Pakistanis (host's figure) incl. suicide assault on GHQ Rawalpindi; Pakistan endured it for 'strategic depth'
US government maintained estimate of 50-100 AQ in Afghanistan for six years until a raid on an AQ camp killed ~150
US military targeting Tajmir Jawad (earliest record found by host)

key_claims: Taliban–al-Qaeda and Taliban–TTP links are 'strong and symbiotic'; the Taliban pays AQ members monthly welfare and issues them passports and national ID cards through Siraj Haqqani's Interior Ministry.

Three dual-hatted AQ-associated figures hold Taliban posts: Qari Baryal (Kapisa governor, northern zone commander), Hafiz Hakim (Nuristan governor), Tajmir Jawad (deputy intelligence chief reporting to Siraj); an unnamed AQ member is MoD training director.
Zawahiri's July 2022 death in a Haqqani-associated Kabul guesthouse exploded the Taliban lie that AQ is not in Afghanistan.
The Haqqanis deliberately seized the interior ministry and intelligence in Aug 2021 to control passports/nationality, enabling foreign fighters to travel or be naturalized.
The Taliban cannot be a CT partner: they fight ISKP only as rivals, have not met Doha CT provisions, and would lie about who is a terrorist.
UN estimates: ~30 AQ core leaders, ~600 AQ members, ~200 AQIS, 4,000-6,000 ISKP (doubled in two years), ~6,000 TTP in Afghanistan; Roggio thinks AQ figures are low.
Pakistan endured ~100,000 dead in the 2007-2015 TTP insurgency for 'strategic depth' and will not break with the Taliban over ~900 casualties a year.
Siraj Haqqani runs meth labs in eastern Afghanistan; the Taliban is effectively a narco-state with untouchables protected by Hibatullah.

Roggio disputes UN emphasis on internal divisions (Baradar–Haqqani feud, Hibatullah sidelining others): Yaqoob (defense) and Siraj (interior) are too powerful to be sidelined, but they defer to Hibatullah as Omar's successor; the Taliban will remain cohesive.
Siraj Haqqani wants to be kingmaker, not king; Hibatullah owes him for reuniting the Taliban after Omar's concealed death (2013-2015).
ISKP leader Sanaullah Ghafari is a former Haqqani Network member; Haqqanis may use ISKP as a cutout.
